sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the centre of the borough along Kinderkamack Road, from Orchard at the top to Center at the bottom, with the Hackensack River and the New Jersey and New York Railroad along the right edge. Oradell Avenue crosses Kinderkamack Road near the middle, and the business block on its south-east corner holds the post office, the First National Bank, a metal works, shops with stores and offices above, and a large brick garage for forty-five cars. The police headquarters and the Oradell Athletic Club stand on the west side of the road, with the fire alarm box near the corner. North of Oradell Avenue, Veloran Avenue runs east-south-east from Kinderkamack Road to the railroad, past a grain store, stables and the Oradell Flour and Grain Company, whose brick storehouse stands against the tracks beside a freight depot. The passenger depot and the American Railway Express office stand between Maple Avenue and the tracks, south of a triangular public park. Maple Avenue runs south from Oradell Avenue behind the east side of Kinderkamack Road, with small frame dwellings on both streets. On the west side, below Church (Hale), stand the Oradell Reformed Church with its hall, the Oradell Public School, and the Church of the Ascension (Episcopal). Orchard crosses the top of the sheet at a slant, with narrow lots of frame dwellings on its south side. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches follow the streets. The sheet is turned about six degrees from north, and a compass rose stands at the left.
notes: Veloran Avenue is Veldran Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Orchard, Church (Hale) and Center are Orchard Street, Church Street and Center Street today.
Kinderkamack Road is drawn about 50 to 55 feet wide between the property lines, narrower than the roughly 75 feet of today's right-of-way; the detector measured it as narrow.

50 ft. Downtown: Kinderkamack Rd from Orchard to Center, Oradell Av, Veloran Av, Church (Hale), Maple Av, N.J. & N.Y. R.R. and passenger depot, Hackensack River on the east. One part. Drawn about -5.5 degrees.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the residential blocks just south of the business centre, between Center Street at the top and Ridgewood Road at the bottom. Kinderkamack Road runs down the west side, with Maple Avenue and Railroad Avenue parallel to it further east, and the double track of the N.J. & N.Y. Railroad curving along the east edge. The two blocks between Kinderkamack Road and Maple Avenue are lined with frame dwellings and private garages on narrow lots; the Delford Fire Department building with its hose tower stands on the east side of Kinderkamack Road near the fire alarm box, and a small metal works sits behind the lots facing Kinderkamack. A brick and frame store building occupies the corner of Kinderkamack Road and Ridgewood Road. Between Maple Avenue and Railroad Avenue the block is mostly dwellings with a few outbuildings and open lots. East of Railroad Avenue are a small office and scales, a coal shed and warehouse along the railroad siding, and a row of houses on lots facing the tracks toward the south. Park Avenue enters from the west as a dashed, unopened line opposite the fire department. Six-inch water pipes are drawn along Kinderkamack Road, Maple Avenue, Railroad Avenue and Ridgewood Road, with hydrants marked. The west margin shows only the edges of the blocks on sheet 7, and the top margin those of sheet 2; the area east of the railroad continues on sheet 10.
notes: Railroad Avenue is now Genther Avenue.
Ridgewood Road is now Ridgewood Avenue.
Center is Center Street today.
Delford Fire Department on Kinderkamack Road.
Pilot sheet for the atlas: detector ink_below_paper 100 (the default 138 found 1 point).
50 ft. Kinderkamack Rd, Maple Av and Railroad Av between Center and Ridgewood Rd; N.J. & N.Y. R.R. on the east. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, is given over almost entirely to the Oradell plant of the Hackensack Water Company on the Hackensack River at the south-east corner of the borough. New Milford Avenue crosses the sheet from west to east just above the middle; Elm runs north from it along the Hackensack Water Co's Intake Canal, and River Road leaves it toward the south-east and crosses the river into the Borough of New Milford. North of New Milford Avenue stand the long filter plant with its laboratories and storage of supplies, a 100,000 gallon wash water tank on concrete pillars, the pumping station and boiler house with their chimney, a repair shop, a gate house and concrete tank, and the large rectangular Settling Reservoir of 12,000,000 gallons, all tied together by a dense web of raw water, clear water, drain and intake pipes drawn as dashed lines. A short intake canal and the main canal bring river water to the suction well. South of the avenue are the coal house on a coal trestle and the bend of the Hackensack River, which also forms the borough line. At the south-west, beside the N.J. & N.Y. Railroad and the New Milford passenger depot, is the Cooper and Demarest Lumber Company with a lumber shed, office and storage sheds. A long block of text at the lower right describes the water company's supply works, pumps and boilers. The land south of the river is left blank with a note to see the map of New Milford.
notes: River Road is now Madison Avenue (New Milford) where it meets New Milford Avenue.
Elm is Elm Street today.
Hackensack Water Company filter plant, pumping station and settling reservoir.
Cooper and Demarest Lumber Company beside the New Milford passenger depot of the N.J. & N.Y. Railroad.
Only three control points, all along New Milford Avenue: placed with a helmert transformation; low confidence.

50 ft. Hackensack Water Co. works: filter plant, pumping station, settling reservoir; New Milford Av, Elm, River Rd, Hackensack River and intake canal, Cooper & Demarest Lumber Co. by the N.J. & N.Y. R.R. One part, few street junctions.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the south end of the borough from Argyle at the top to the borough limits at the bottom, between Kinderkamack Road on the left and the New Jersey and New York Railroad on the right. Four streets cross the built-up area from top to bottom: Kinderkamack Road, Beverly Road and Windsor Road run south, and Argyle, Berkshire and Clinton cross them. The blocks hold small frame dwellings on narrow numbered lots, most of them set at the back of deep plots, with a few outbuildings. The only larger buildings are on the east side of Kinderkamack Road: two garages, one for 45 cars and one for 50 cars, with offices and stores beside them, and a small frame, brick and concrete building at the borough limits at the bottom. Mackay Avenue, Banta Place and Winne Avenue come in from the left across Kinderkamack Road, with the blocks beyond them left blank for sheet 6. Six-inch and 24-inch water pipes run along Kinderkamack Road and the cross streets. A row of narrow lots lies between Windsor Road and the railroad, which runs diagonally down the right side with several tracks. The borough limits are drawn along the bottom edge, and the land below them is lettered Borough of Riverside. The sheet is turned about eighteen degrees from north, with a compass rose at the top.
notes: Argyle, Berkshire and Clinton are Argyle Street, Berkshire Street and Morcom Terrace today; Clinton is matched to Morcom Terrace by position and is a probable renaming.
The borough limits at the bottom of the sheet separate Oradell from Riverside, now part of the Borough of River Edge.
Banta Place does not appear in the OpenStreetMap street list.

50 ft. Kinderkamack Rd, Beverly Rd, Windsor Rd between Argyle and the Riverside (River Edge) borough limits; Berkshire, Clinton; railroad on the east. One part. Turned about -18 degrees. Clinton is matched to modern Morcom Terrace by position.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the south-western part of the borough, from Brookside Avenue and Broadway Boulevard at the top left to Argyle at the bottom right. Kinderkamack Road enters at the top from sheet 7, bends south-east past Brookside Avenue and Lake Avenue, and runs down the right side of the sheet, curving again at High and New Milford Avenue. Elizabeth runs south from Kinderkamack Road through the middle of the sheet, crossed by Taylor Avenue, Edwin Avenue, Fletcher Avenue and Mackay Avenue. West of it the blocks between Pyle and Poplar Avenue, Elm Avenue and Grand Avenue are divided into deep narrow lots, many still without buildings. Between Elizabeth and Kinderkamack Road are Reis Avenue, Prior Court and Elliot Court, with rows of small dwellings on Reis Avenue. At the upper left a contractor's yard, a garage, a blacksmith shop and an auto repair shop stand between Westervelt Place and Elizabeth. Grant Avenue and Lincoln Avenue run north-east through a district of detached dwellings and a filling station, and a large field with a few farm buildings lies between New Milford Avenue and the railroad. At the right the New Jersey and New York Railroad runs beside the Hackensack River. Beverly Road and Windsor Road enter at the bottom right, where Argyle joins the sheet to sheet 5. A street east of Kinderkamack Road is lettered Not Named. Several block numbers carry the later renumbering in parentheses, and water pipes of 6 and 20 inches follow the streets.
notes: Edwin Avenue is Schaefer Avenue in OpenStreetMap, matched by position.
Elizabeth, High and Pyle are Elizabeth Street, High Street and Pyle Street today; Argyle is Argyle Street.
Broadway Boulevard is Martin Avenue today, and Maple Avenue meets Brookside Avenue at the top of the sheet.
Elm Avenue, Grand Avenue, Summit Avenue South, Grant Avenue and Banta Place were not matched to modern streets and are not used as control.
Kinderkamack Road, High and Lake Avenue curve at the top of the sheet; their junctions with Kinderkamack Road were not accepted as control points.

100 ft. South-west Oradell: Kinderkamack Rd, Broadway Blvd, Lake, Taylor, Edwin, Fletcher, Mackay Avs, Elizabeth, High, Reis, Prior Ct, Elliot Ct, Poplar, Elm, Grand, Summit Av South, Banta Pl, Grant, Lincoln, New Milford Av, Beverly Rd, Argyle. One part. Turned about -8 degrees. Edwin Av is modern Schaefer Avenue (by position). Pequot, Banta Pl, Elm Av, Grand Av and Summit Av South have no OpenStreetMap match here and are not used.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the west side of the borough between Prospect Avenue and Kinderkamack Road, from Oradell Avenue at the top to Broadway Boulevard at the bottom. The cross streets are Oradell Avenue, Church, Center, Park Avenue, Ridgewood Road, Cooper Avenue and Broadway Boulevard; Union and John run north and south between Ridgewood Road and Broadway Boulevard, each with a jog at Broadway Boulevard, and Pyle begins at the bottom right. The large block between Church and Center is the grounds of Oradell High School, a brick building with an auditorium at the north end and a gymnasium at the south. The block between Oradell Avenue and Church holds a few frame dwellings on lots numbered as a subdivision. South of Center the land is laid out in long rows of narrow numbered building lots, most of them still vacant in 1930, with scattered dwellings and private garages; houses are more frequent along Ridgewood Road and toward Kinderkamack Road, where a filling station and garage and a second filling station stand at the corner of Ridgewood Road. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes are drawn along the streets with hydrants marked. The west margin beyond Prospect Avenue is marked as no exposure, and the right side of the sheet, behind a heavy line, holds a separate inset of the blocks east of Kinderkamack Road (part 2).
notes: Union between Ridgewood Road and Cooper Avenue is now Carolina Drive; south of Broadway Boulevard it is Union Street.
Broadway Boulevard is now Martin Avenue in this area.
Ridgewood Road is now Ridgewood Avenue; Center is Center Street; Church is Church Street; John is John Street; Pyle is Pyle Street.
Oradell High School between Church and Center.
Union and John each jog at Broadway Boulevard; both offsets are drawn and both are used as control points.

100 ft. Two parts: main (Prospect Av to Kinderkamack Rd, Oradell Av to Broadway Blvd: Church, Center, Park, Ridgewood Rd, Cooper Av, Union, John, Pyle; Oradell High School) and an inset at upper right behind a heavy line (Ridgewood Rd, Kinderkamack Rd, Maple Av, Railroad Av, Brookside Av) with its own north arrow.

sheet-7-2.description: The inset at the upper right of sheet 7 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, set off from the main map by a heavy line and given its own north arrow, shows the small district east of Kinderkamack Road between Ridgewood Road at the top and Brookside Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about ten degrees from the main map. Kinderkamack Road runs down the west side of the inset, with Cooper Avenue and Broadway Boulevard meeting it from the west; Maple Avenue runs diagonally through the middle and Railroad Avenue along the east side, and Brookside Avenue closes the area on the south-east. The two triangular blocks are filled with frame dwellings and private garages on narrow numbered lots. A filling station stands at the corner of Kinderkamack Road and Ridgewood Road, and a row of brick stores faces Kinderkamack Road near Brookside Avenue. A few stores and a small brick building lie along Maple Avenue. Six-inch water pipes are drawn in Ridgewood Road, Maple Avenue and Brookside Avenue, with hydrants marked. The blocks north of Ridgewood Road belong to sheet 3 and those south of Brookside Avenue to sheet 6, which carry the adjoining areas at their own scales.
notes: Railroad Avenue is now Genther Avenue.
Ridgewood Road is now Ridgewood Avenue.
The inset is drawn at a rotation about ten degrees different from the main part of the sheet.

100 ft. Two parts: main (Prospect Av to Kinderkamack Rd, Oradell Av to Broadway Blvd: Church, Center, Park, Ridgewood Rd, Cooper Av, Union, John, Pyle; Oradell High School) and an inset at upper right behind a heavy line (Ridgewood Rd, Kinderkamack Rd, Maple Av, Railroad Av, Brookside Av) with its own north arrow.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the north-western part of the borough from Soldier Hill Road at the top, where the Borough of Emerson begins, to Oradell Avenue at the bottom, and from beyond Birchtree Lane on the left to Seminole on the right. The sheet is turned about twenty degrees from north, as the compass rose at the right shows. Most of the area is a regular grid of narrow numbered lots laid out along Austin Avenue, Clinton Avenue, Lenox Avenue, Lotus Avenue, Amaryllis Avenue, Woodland Avenue and Midland Road, crossed by Summit Avenue, Pequot, Iroquois and Seminole. Few of the lots are built on: small frame dwellings stand in clusters on the blocks near Seminole and Summit Avenue, and one or two larger buildings, among them a few brick-coloured buildings on Woodland Avenue and near Lotus Avenue, are coloured pink. West of Summit Avenue the blocks around Birchtree Lane are large unsubdivided tracts with a few houses, and a curved road with a six-inch water pipe runs from Soldier Hill Road down to Summit Avenue. Green Tree Lane is lettered as a stub off Seminole at the right edge. Oradell Avenue closes the bottom of the sheet, with the blocks below it left to the adjoining sheet. Block numbers are printed with the later numbering in parentheses. The margin above and below the drawing carries the word Exposure.
notes: Birchtree Lane (Cheyenne) is Birchtree Road in OpenStreetMap; Green Tree Lane is Greentree Lane.
Pequot and Iroquois, and Iroquois south of Soldier Hill Road, do not appear as streets in the OpenStreetMap extract; only Iroquois Street at the top was matched.
Soldier Hill Road, Summit, Seminole and Iroquois are Soldier Hill Road, Summit Avenue, Seminole Street and Iroquois Street today.
Soldier Hill Road is the borough limit with Emerson at the top of the sheet.

100 ft. North-west: Soldier Hill Rd to Oradell Av, Birchtree La (Cheyenne), Summit Av, Pequot, Iroquois, Seminole; Austin, Clinton, Lenox, Lotus, Amaryllis, Woodland Avs, Midland Rd. One part. Turned about -20 degrees. Birchtree La is Birchtree Road, Green Tree La is Greentree Lane.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the north-eastern part of the borough from Soldier Hill Road at the top, where the sheet is marked no exposure, to Oradell Avenue at the bottom, and from Seminole at the left to the New Jersey and New York Railroad and the Oradell Reservoir at the right. The sheet is turned about twenty degrees from north, with the compass rose in the middle. Prospect Avenue and Kinderkamack Road run down the sheet side by side, diverging toward the south, and Green Tree Lane, Lotus Avenue, Amaryllis Avenue, Woodland Avenue and Midland Road cross to the left of them, with Lotus Avenue and Orchard also running between the two. The blocks west of Prospect Avenue are laid out in narrow numbered lots and hold scattered frame dwellings. The area between the two main roads is mostly large farm tracts, with the houses of the older properties near Soldier Hill Road, and a church of Christ, Scientist stands on Kinderkamack Road at Lotus Avenue. Rows of narrow lots line Lotus Avenue and Orchard, with dwellings set well back. East of Kinderkamack Road the long lots run to the railroad, with a few houses, and a street east of Kinderkamack Road is lettered Not Named. The Oradell Reservoir of the Hackensack Water Company lies along the right edge, with the owner named beside it. Six-inch and twelve-inch water pipes follow the main streets. The streets at the bottom edge continue on sheet 7.
notes: Green Tree Lane is Greentree Lane in OpenStreetMap; Orchard and Seminole are Orchard Street and Seminole Street today.
The reservoir is lettered Oradell Reservoir, Hackensack Water Co., Owner.
Greentree Lane at Prospect Avenue and Seminole Street at Soldier Hill Road were excluded from control as unreliable.
Kinderkamack Road is drawn about 50 feet wide between its lines, narrower than the 75 feet of today's right-of-way.

100 ft. Soldier Hill Rd to Oradell Av between Seminole and the railroad: Green Tree La, Lotus, Amaryllis, Woodland Avs, Midland Rd, Prospect Av, Kinderkamack Rd, Orchard; Oradell Reservoir on the east. One part. Turned about -20 degrees.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the part of the borough east of the Hackensack River, from the river and the N.J. & N.Y. Railroad on the west to the New Milford borough line on the east. Oradell Avenue crosses the sheet from the bridge over the river at the left, where Veloran Avenue comes in, to the right edge. North of it are large lots along the streets leading north, a short section of 1st Street curving toward sheet 11, and a street marked not opened. South of Oradell Avenue, Grove and Demarest run south through blocks of small frame dwellings on narrow lots, and Elm runs south-west to the bottom of the sheet, where it meets Grove near the river. Hasbrook Boulevard leaves Elm toward the east, and Harrison, Grand and Center cross the south-east corner, where the borough limits cut across the blocks; Golden Gate Avenue runs south from Center along the line. St. Joseph's Roman Catholic Church and its rectory stand at Harrison and Grand, with a note that they are also shown on the New Milford map. A street between Grove and Elm is marked not opened. The Hackensack River winds through the western third of the sheet in wide meanders, with the railroad along its west bank; Center Street and Railroad Avenue are lettered at the left margin where they belong to sheet 3. The land beyond the borough limits at the right is left blank with a note to see the New Milford map.
notes: Hasbrook Boulevard is spelled Hasbrouck Boulevard today.
Veloran Avenue is spelled Veldran Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Grove, Demarest, Elm, Harrison, Grand and Center are Grove Street, Demarest Avenue, Elm Street, Harrison Street, Grand Street and Center Street today.
St. Joseph's R.C. Church and rectory at Harrison and Grand.
Grand between Grove and Elm is marked not opened.
100 ft. East of the Hackensack River: Oradell Av, Grove, Demarest, Elm, Hasbrook Blvd, 1st St, Harrison, Grand, Center, Golden Gate Av; New Milford borough line on the east. One part.

sheet-11-1.description: The main part of sheet 11 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north straight up, covers the north-east corner of the borough east of the Hackensack River and the Oradell Reservoir. Oradell Avenue crosses the lower middle of the sheet from the left edge to Grand Avenue. North of it, 2nd Street and 3rd Street run north to 1st Street, which curves across the top of the developed area from the left edge to Grand Avenue, and Grand Avenue runs north-north-east to Haworth Drive at the top of the sheet. The blocks between Oradell Avenue and 1st Street are laid out in narrow numbered lots with frame dwellings and private garages spread thinly among them, a little denser along 2nd Street; the lots north of 1st Street front a single row of houses, with no exposure beyond. A short street east of Grand Avenue near Oradell Avenue is marked not named. Below Oradell Avenue are a few dwellings and large unbuilt plots, and in the south-east the large lot of the Oradell Riding Academy with its stables and outbuildings. The Borough of Haworth line runs diagonally across the upper left, below a strip of the Oradell Reservoir, and the borough limits at the bottom separate Oradell from the Borough of New Milford, whose streets (Grove Avenue, Prospect Avenue, Summit Avenue, Eagle Avenue and Boulevard) are indicated with a note to see the New Milford map. A heavy line divides this part from the strip along Kinderkamack Road on the right (part 2).
notes: Grand Avenue is now Grant Avenue.
Haworth Drive at the top of Grand Avenue has no counterpart under that name today in this area.
Oradell Riding Academy south of Oradell Avenue.
1st Street, 2nd Street and 3rd Street keep their names.

100 ft. Two parts: left (1st, 2nd, 3rd Sts, Grand Av, Oradell Av, Haworth Drive) and right behind a heavy line (Kinderkamack Rd north to the Emerson line, Soldier Hill Rd, Kinderkamack Inn, railroad) drawn with its own north arrow.

sheet-11-2.description: The right-hand part of sheet 11 of the 1930 Oradell atlas, set off from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, shows the long strip of Kinderkamack Road north of Soldier Hill Road toward the Emerson line, turned about sixteen degrees on the page. Kinderkamack Road runs the full height of the strip with a twelve-inch water pipe in it, Soldier Hill Road meets it from the west at the bottom, and the double track of the N.J. & N.Y. Railroad runs parallel along the east edge. The land on both sides is divided into a few large numbered lots and is almost empty; the main building is the Kinderkamack Inn, a frame building on the east side of the road near the top, and a few dwellings and outbuildings stand on the west side along the heavy line. Long narrow lots between the road and the railroad are numbered but unbuilt. The edges of the strip are marked no exposure, and the blocks south of Soldier Hill Road continue on sheet 9.
notes: Kinderkamack Inn on Kinderkamack Road.
Placed from one control point (Kinderkamack Road and Soldier Hill Road) with the rotation from its drawn lines and the atlas scale assumed: low confidence, especially at the north end.

100 ft. Two parts: left (1st, 2nd, 3rd Sts, Grand Av, Oradell Av, Haworth Drive) and right behind a heavy line (Kinderkamack Rd north to the Emerson line, Soldier Hill Rd, Kinderkamack Inn, railroad) drawn with its own north arrow.
